name: BangDB
tagline: Converged C/C++ NoSQL platform mixing key-value, documents, time-series, stream processing, graph and ML.
description: BangDB, from IQLECT, is a C/C++ NoSQL engine that tries to replace a stack of separate systems: key-value and document tables, wide and time-series tables, an S3-like store for large objects, continuous stream processing with sliding windows and complex event processing, a graph layer queried with a modified Cypher, and in-database model training and prediction. It ships as an embedded library or a client/server database (primary/replica), with a quasi-SQL CLI, plus a hosted BangDB Cloud and the Ampere no-code app platform aimed at real-time analytics, IoT and log monitoring. BangDB 2.0 binaries and a Docker image are free to download, but the core source is not published, and its performance claims are vendor benchmarks.

pricing.notes: Server binaries and Docker image are free to download (registration encouraged); BangDB Cloud and the Ampere platform are paid, with a one-month app trial. Deep-learning features need the Enterprise Edition.

scale.notes: Embedded or primary/replica server today; a peer-to-peer distributed mode has been described as upcoming.

strengths: One engine covers documents, time-series, streams, graph and ML scoring
Stream processing with sliding windows, CEP and running statistics built in
Same API for embedded and client/server deployments
Vendor offers a hosted cloud and no-code app platform on top
weaknesses: Core source is not public; free binaries only
Small community and limited third-party documentation
useCases: Real-time IoT and sensor stream analytics with alerts
Log and clickstream monitoring with anomaly detection
Edge or device deployments using the embedded flavour
notIdealFor: Large multi-node clusters needing automatic sharding
